payload.rationale: Without a current forecast for September 19, 2026, I must rely on historical climatology for Austin, Texas. The average high temperature in mid-to-late September is typically in the upper 80s to low 90s. A high of 98-99°F is above average but occurs occasionally during late-season heat waves. Because the target is a narrow two-degree band (98°F to 99°F) on the warmer tail of the distribution, the baseline probability is low. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is if the actual forecast is significantly cooler (e.g., a cold front bringing highs in the 70s or 80s) or hotter (100+°F), making this narrow band highly unlikely. The strongest reason this could be too low is if a heat wave is currently forecast with expected highs right around 98-99°F, which would make the probability much higher than the climatological baseline.
limitations: No current weather forecast data is available for the target date.
Reliance on historical climatology rather than real-time meteorological models.
